findings.source_passage: look here,—three peaks as proud as Lucifer. The firm tower, that is Ahab; the volcano, that is Ahab
findings.why_it_matters: The opening line of Ahab's soliloquy—'There's something ever egotistical in mountain-tops and towers'—is present, but the crucial 'look here,—three peaks as proud as Lucifer' is cut. 'Proud as Lucifer' is the interpretive keystone linking Ahab's egotism to satanic pride, a phrase the critical tradition consistently returns to.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'look here,—three peaks as proud as Lucifer' verbatim before 'The firm tower, that is Ahab.'

findings.source_passage: Humph! in my poor, insignificant opinion, I regard this as queer.
findings.why_it_matters: This self-deflating aside is a voice-establishing marker for Stubb's comic register; its absence flattens the transition into his list of doubloons and removes a key tonal signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Humph! in my poor, insignificant opinion, I regard this as queer.' after the nine-fathoms-long observation.

findings.source_passage: Signs and wonders, eh? Pity if there is nothing wonderful in signs, and significant in wonders! There's a clue somewhere; wait a bit; hist—hark! By Jove, I have it!
findings.source_locator: Stubb's soliloquy, mid-section, before the zodiac reading
findings.why_it_matters: This punning, self-amused rhetorical buildup is the hinge of Stubb's entire speech and a signature moment of his comic voice; without it, his zodiac reading appears unannounced and loses its performative energy.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'Signs and wonders, eh? Pity if...' passage and the 'By Jove, I have it!' transition verbatim before the zodiac reading begins.

findings.source_passage: But stop; here comes little King-Post; dodge round the try-works, now, and let's hear what he'll have to say.
findings.source_locator: Stubb's soliloquy, closing lines before Flask
findings.why_it_matters: Stubb's stage-managing commentary between readers ('dodge round the try-works') is a formal device structuring the chapter as a sequence of interpretive performances; reducing Flask's entry to a bare attribution destroys this frame.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Stubb's transition commentary—'But stop; here comes little King-Post; dodge round the try-works, now'—before Flask's lines.

findings.source_passage: Wonder if he means me?—complimentary!—poor lad!—I could go hang myself. Any way, for the present, I'll quit Pip's vicinity. I can stand the rest, for they have plain wits; but he's too crazy-witty for my sanity.
findings.source_locator: Stubb's commentary after Pip's first recitation
findings.why_it_matters: The 'I could go hang myself' and the full emotional aside are collapsed into a skeletal paraphrase, erasing Stubb's mixture of comic self-deprecation and genuine unsettlement at Pip—a key register moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Wonder if he means me?—complimentary!—poor lad!—I could go hang myself' verbatim as part of Stubb's internal reaction to Pip.

findings.source_passage: old Manxman—the old hearse-driver, he must have been, that is, before he took to the sea. He luffs up before the doubloon; halloa, and goes round on the other side of the mast; why, there's a horse-shoe nailed on that side
findings.why_it_matters: The Manxman's route around the mast to the horse-shoe—and Stubb's 'old hearse-driver' epithet—establishes the ominous context for his prophecy; without it, his prediction of the lion-sign loses its carefully constructed dramatic frame.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Manxman's circuit of the mast and the horse-shoe discovery as narrated through Stubb's voice before the Manxman's speech.

findings.source_passage: Ho! more and more. This way comes Pip—poor boy! would he had died, or I; he's half horrible to me. He too has been watching all of these interpreters—myself included—and look now, he comes to read, with that unearthly idiot face.
findings.why_it_matters: Only a fragment is kept; the critical phrase 'He too has been watching all of these interpreters—myself included' is absent, removing the meta-interpretive frame that makes Pip's grammar-conjugation into a comment on the whole chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'He too has been watching all of these interpreters—myself included' before Pip approaches the coin.

findings.source_passage: the green miser'll hoard ye soon!
findings.why_it_matters: This line—evoking the sea as miser—is a small but distinctive image in Pip's visionary speech; its omission slightly thins the closing passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'the green miser'll hoard ye soon!' after 'Oh, the gold! the precious, precious, gold!'

summary: The draft preserves major soliloquies in skeleton form but erases the between-speaker stage-managing commentary that gives the chapter its meta-interpretive architecture, cuts the 'proud as Lucifer' keystone phrase, and flattens Stubb's comic voice-establishing asides—collectively six medium and one high finding.
